fields.description:
Update AGENTS.md + docs (epic items 6–7) once the ADR (deft-evolutive-mosasaur) and trusted-env
registration land: require using the MCP server for all rebar operations EXCEPT operations that need
local code (testing, investigation, debugging, validation), and state the certified-op policy
correctly. Single concern: guidance + user-facing docs — no server/infra behavior here.

## Scope + rationale
1. **AGENTS.md MCP-required policy**: a rule that rebar tracker operations go through the MCP server,
   with the explicit carve-out for local-code ops (test/investigate/debug/validate). Because this
   introduces a new prohibition ("don't drive the tracker by ad-hoc local CLI when MCP is
   available"), do the new-prohibition **consumer scan**: enumerate the existing guidance/workflows
   that tell agents to run `rebar ...` tracker ops locally and reconcile each. The rule is written in
   AGENTS.md (rebar's canonical cross-vendor guidance) as an **umbrella** that explicitly governs the
   downstream guidance surfaces (`docs/`, `templates/`, `.agents/rules/`, packaged `rebar explain`
   guides, example skills): a `rebar <verb>` shown for a tracker op names the operation and routes
   through the MCP server when configured, so those surfaces are reconciled by reference rather than
   individually rewritten. The non-doc surfaces (templates/packaged-guides/vendor-rules/skills) get a
   per-file textual sweep under a linked follow-up ticket; this leaf edits AGENTS.md + docs only.
2. **Certified-op wording correction**: certified **plan-review** and **completion-verifier** ops
   (the only two op-cert kinds, ADR 0049) route through the MCP server and are enforceable because
   the box is a registered trusted signing environment (the trusted-env slice). **Code review is the
   Gerrit `LLM-Review` vote, NOT an op-cert** — record the code-review-vs-op-cert correction (the
   epic's item-7 "code review ... certified through the MCP server" phrasing) per **ADR 0104**
   (deft-evolutive-mosasaur, decision 3), so guidance doesn't imply a nonexistent code-review
   op-cert. Enforcement of the certified ops is **enableable but deferred**: describe them as
   enforceable-when-enabled via the trusted-env mechanism, and cite the operator flip runbook
   (`infra/runbooks/mcp-opcert-enforcement-flip.md`) — do NOT claim enforcement is live.
3. **docs/mcp-auth.md**: fill the §7 "AWS-specific deployment" gap with the ADR-decided recipe
   (nginx `/mcp/` TLS edge + `static` verifier + per-client bearer). Surface the client-connection
   guide (copilot/codex/claude config shapes from olm's `docs/mcp-client-setup.md`) from
   docs/mcp-auth.md, which currently lacks the link.

## Prior-art / doc-drift check (blocking prior-art overlay)
Git history shows the hand-authored MCP docs carry modest recurring upkeep; keep the AWS recipe and
client guide close to the single-sourced config keys the ADR names so they don't drift. Match the
existing docs/mcp-auth.md structure rather than inventing a parallel doc; reference the already-landed
`docs/mcp-client-setup.md` and `infra/runbooks/*` rather than duplicating them.

## Testing / Verification
Docs-only leaf: no behavioral tests. Each acceptance criterion below carries its proof (a recorded
tracker artifact or a greppable command). Run the greppable oracles plus `make lint` before pushing.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] AGENTS.md states the MCP-required rule + the local-code carve-out, written as an umbrella that
  names the downstream guidance surfaces it governs
  (checked: `grep -niE 'MCP server|local-code|carve-out' AGENTS.md` shows the rule + carve-out).
- [x] The consumer scan is recorded as the primary oracle: `rebar show inadequate-hydrated-starling`
  carries a comment enumerating each pre-existing tracker-op "run rebar locally" instruction surface
  and its reconciliation disposition (umbrella-covered / carve-out / follow-up ticket). A supporting
  `grep -rniE 'rebar (claim|transition|link|review-plan)' AGENTS.md docs/ .agents/ templates/`
  lists the candidate lines the reviewer confirms are each covered — the comment, not the grep, is
  the pass/fail record.
- [x] A follow-up ticket for the per-file reconciliation sweep of the non-doc surfaces
  (templates/, packaged `rebar explain` guides, `.agents/rules/`, example skills) is created and
  linked `discovered_from` this ticket (checked: `rebar show inadequate-hydrated-starling` lists an
  inbound `discovered_from` child).
- [x] The certified-op section names plan-review + completion-verifier as MCP-routed/enforceable-via
  trusted-env and code-review as the Gerrit vote (NOT an op-cert)
  (checked: `grep -niE 'plan-review|completion-verifier|LLM-Review' AGENTS.md` shows both op-cert
  kinds plus the Gerrit vote framing).
- [x] No reference asserting a code-review op-cert survives in guidance
  (checked: `grep -rniE 'code[- ]review.{0,40}op-?cert|code[- ]review.{0,40}certif' AGENTS.md docs/`
  returns only the ADR 0104 correction record, never an assertion that one exists).
- [x] Guidance describes certified-op enforcement as deferred/enableable, not live
  (checked: `grep -niE 'enforcement.*(defer|enable)|mcp-opcert-enforcement-flip' AGENTS.md` shows the
  deferred framing + runbook citation).
- [x] docs/mcp-auth.md §7 contains the AWS deploy recipe with the ADR-named config keys
  (checked: `grep -niE 'AWS|http_tls_at_edge|auth_static_tokens_file|auth_strategies' docs/mcp-auth.md`
  shows the recipe with the keys).
- [x] A client-connection guide documenting the three client config shapes is reachable from
  docs/mcp-auth.md (checked: `grep -ni 'mcp-client-setup' docs/mcp-auth.md` links the guide, which
  documents the copilot/codex/claude shapes).

## Compat / rollback
Docs-only; rollback = revert the doc edits. No behavior change.

Depends on: deft-evolutive-mosasaur (ADR 0104 decides routing/auth), and the trusted-env registration
slice (guidance claims certified ops are enforceable via MCP, which is only true once the box is a
trusted env).
